overview:
scheduler-core

A tiny, dependency-free library for reserving rooms over time. The core types are Interval (a span of time) and Booking (a room reserved for an interval), and the Schedule class enforces one rule: no two bookings in the same room may overlap.

Times are represented as minutes since midnight, so 09:00 is 540 and 10:00 is 600.
guide/intervals:
Time intervals

An Interval is half-open: { start, end } covers every minute from start up to but not including end. A booking for 09:00–10:00 therefore occupies 09:00, 09:30, 09:59 — but releases the room exactly at 10:00.

This convention is what makes back-to-back bookings work: a 10:00–11:00 booking begins at the precise minute the 09:00–10:00 booking ends, and the two do not conflict. See overlaps for the rule.
api/overlaps:
overlaps(a, b)

Returns true when intervals a and b share at least one minute, and false otherwise.

Because intervals are half-open, two intervals that merely touch — where one ends at the exact minute the other begins — do not overlap. For example, 09:00–10:00 and 10:00–11:00 are back-to-back, not a conflict, so overlaps returns false for that boundary pair.

This boundary rule (touching is not overlapping) is the single most common source of off-by-one scheduling bugs — an implementation that uses < where it needs <= will wrongly reject back-to-back bookings.
api/book:
Schedule.book(room, title, interval)

Reserves room for interval and returns the created Booking. Throws if the interval overlaps an existing booking in the same room.

A booking whose interval merely touches an existing one (its start equals the other's end, or vice versa) is not a conflict and is accepted.
